Saffron Rice Cake with Barberries and Chicken (Tahchin)

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 6-8Prep 45 minCook 1 hour 15 min

Tahchin is a beautiful and flavorful layered Persian rice dish, often served for special occasions and celebrations. For Yalda Night, the winter solstice, it graces the table as a symbol of warmth, abundance, and the vibrant colors of the season, especially with its golden crust and ruby red barberries.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (600 g) Basmati rice
  • 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts
  • 1.5 cups (360 g) full-fat plain yogurt (Greek yogurt works well)
  • 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
  • 2 large egg yolks
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) dried barberries (Zereshk)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil or ghee, plus 2 tablespoons for barberries
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter (optional, for richness)
  • 1 medium onion, chopped
  • 1 teaspoon turmeric
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • 1 tablespoon granulated sugar (for barberries)
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) slivered pistachios or almonds (optional, for garnish)

Method

  1. Prepare Saffron: Grind saffron threads with a mortar and pestle. Steep in 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water or 2-3 ice cubes for at least 15 minutes to release color and flavor.
  2. Cook Chicken: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté chopped onion until translucent. Add chicken pieces, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook until chicken is lightly browned. Add 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until cooked through. Shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces and set aside.
  3. Par-boil Rice: Wash rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the washed rice and cook for 7-10 minutes, or until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center (al dente). Drain immediately in a colander and rinse briefly with cool water to stop cooking.
  4. Prepare Yogurt Mixture: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, egg yolks, 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the prepared saffron water, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of black pepper.
  5. Combine Rice and Yogurt: Gently fold about 3 cups (approx. 450 g) of the par-boiled rice into the yogurt mixture until well combined. This will be the bottom layer.
  6. Assemble Tahchin: Choose a non-stick pot with a tight-fitting lid (a 10-inch/25 cm pot works well). Pour 1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil into the pot and swirl to coat the bottom and sides. If using butter, add it now.
  7. Layer 1 (Tahdig): Spread the yogurt-rice mixture evenly over the bottom of the pot, pressing down gently to form a compact layer.
  8. Layer 2 (Chicken): Arrange the shredded chicken evenly over the yogurt-rice layer.
  9. Layer 3 (Remaining Rice): Gently mound the remaining plain par-boiled rice over the chicken. Create a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape. Pour the remaining saffron water over the top of the rice.
  10. Cook Tahchin: Cover the pot with a lid, preferably wrapped in a clean kitchen towel to absorb steam. Cook on medium-high heat for 10-15 minutes until steam builds up. Then reduce heat to low and cook for an additional 50-60 minutes, or until a golden crust (tahdig) forms at the bottom.
  11. Prepare Barberries: While the tahchin cooks, melt 2 tablespoons oil or butter in a small pan over low heat. Add barberries and sugar. Sauté for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until plump and glossy (do not burn). Remove from heat.
  12. Serve: Once cooked, remove the pot from heat and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. Place a large serving platter over the pot and carefully invert the tahchin onto the platter. Garnish with the prepared barberries and optional slivered pistachios or almonds. Serve warm.

Tips

  • For an extra crispy tahdig, ensure the oil is hot before adding the first layer of rice and don't rush the initial high-heat cooking.
  • If you prefer a vegetarian version, omit the chicken and add sautéed mushrooms or eggplant slices instead.
  • The quality of saffron makes a big difference; use good quality threads for the best color and aroma.
